messages.content:
Risk: Dangerous Content
Description: Content that may cause harm to oneself and/or others, including instructions for violence, self-harm, or dangerous activities
Concern: None
Policy: Violence

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0018.000: Poison AI Model - ATLAS — Adversaries may manipulate an AI model's weights to change it's behavior or performance, resulting in a poisoned model.
Adversaries may poison a model by by directly manipulating its weights, training the model on poisoned data, further fine-tuning the model, or otherwise interfering with its training process.

The change in behavior of poisoned models may be limited to targeted categories in predictive AI models, or targeted topics, concepts, or facts in generative AI models, or aim for a general performance degradation. [found by 3/4 queries]
  Siblings: Embed Malware - ATLAS, Modify AI Model Architecture - ATLAS
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts. [found by 2/4 queries]
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#ThreatsOfViolence: Threats of Violence — Communication of intent to inflict harm or damage to create fear, even if not carried out. [found by 2/4 queries]
  Siblings: Homicide, Glorification of Violence, Weapons Use
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0048.002: Societal Harm - ATLAS — Societal harms might generate harmful outcomes that reach either the general public or specific vulnerable groups such as the exposure of children to vulgar content. [found by 2/4 queries]
  Siblings: User Harm - ATLAS, Reputational Harm - ATLAS, Financial Harm - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0010.003: Model - ATLAS — AI-enabled systems often rely on open sourced models in various ways.
Most commonly, the victim organization may be using these models for fine tuning.
These models will be downloaded from an external source and then used as the base for the model as it is tuned on a smaller, private dataset.
Loading models often requires executing some saved code in the form of a saved model file.
These can be compromised with traditional malware, or through some adversarial AI techniques. [found by 2/4 queries]
  Siblings: AI Software - ATLAS, Hardware - ATLAS, Data - ATLAS

axes.rationale: The risk centers around content that can cause harm, aligning with the definition of dangerous information as knowledge or instructions leading to physical harm when executed by untrained individuals.
The risk encompasses content that may incite violence or threats of harm, directly corresponding to the concept of threats of violence.
